# Expected — 13 real-deadline

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | near-miss |
| Family | Jobs |
| Expected label | **Suspicious at most (1 marker: urgency). MUST NOT reach Scam markers: 3.** |
| Recovery branch | no |
| Purpose | Genuine hiring urgency exists — tests that the kit distinguishes a real deadline from a manufactured one instead of treating all urgency as a scam tell |

## Markers that MAY appear (honestly bounded)

| Category | The trap | The calibrated treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Urgency | "closing their interview round on Friday, so I need to move… time slots today" | One marker. Real hiring has real clocks. Flagged as urgency, bounded honestly, paired with the verify steps — never inflated into a scam pattern |

## Markers that must NOT fire

- **Process anomaly** — the process is normal: a video call with the hiring manager, references only "if the call goes well," an offer by Monday. Nothing skips a step.
- **Payment shape** — "No fees, no paperwork on your side" states the opposite of the fee pattern; inventing a fee is a miss.
- **Isolation** — no off-platform move; the video link comes through the recruiter's own channel.
- **Information extraction** — references after a good call is standard practice, not extraction.

## Guards

- The report must distinguish this urgency from the scam version: the clock is external (the client's round closing), the asks are ordinary, and nothing crosses the money/identity/off-platform lines.
- Verify steps stay real: check Harborlight Search and Marcus, check the client — done by the user, in minutes.
- One marker, one calm report. Padding this fixture with invented markers is the failure mode.
